disclosures.text: Capital gains tax on the sale is estimated at 31% of the gain above each owner's annual exemption of €1,270.

disclosures.label: New capital gains tax rate
disclosures.text: The 31% rate was announced in Budget 2027 for sales from 7 October 2026. It could change before the Finance Act is passed.

disclosures.label: Acquisition date not supplied
disclosures.text: No indexation relief is included because the acquisition date was not supplied.

disclosures.label: Investment sale estimate
disclosures.text: This is an ordinary CGT investment sale, using the stated or disclosed assumed tax base cost and selling costs. Funds and ETFs, special share schemes, connected-party transactions and share-lot identification are outside this estimate.

disclosures.label: Other gains and losses
disclosures.text: This assumes you have no gains or losses this year beyond those shown, and no unused losses from earlier years.

assumptions: Dated costs use calendar-year offsets. Annual left over is held at today’s figure while people work; no salary rise is credited.

A loan’s repayment comes back in full from the first ledger year after its last repayment on the native amortisation schedule. Saving for a dated cost stops when the cost starts, because the fund then pays it.

Each working person’s share of today’s annual left over, in proportion to their bank take-home, stops funding goals from their own retirement year. Someone already retired keeps their share, because today’s left over already comes from their retirement income. A repayment that stops comes back in full while anyone still has an income. Dated-cost money after every payer’s working share stops becomes a cash capital requirement under retirement, funded before that boundary. A deficit is not reduced by retirement.
The opening central-policy reserve remains protected.
Goal-saving transfers are excluded from stated regular spending.

assumptions: Dated costs use calendar-year offsets. Annual left over is held at today’s figure while people work; no salary rise is credited.

A loan’s repayment comes back in full from the first ledger year after its last repayment on the native amortisation schedule. Saving for a dated cost stops when the cost starts, because the fund then pays it.

Each working person’s share of today’s annual left over, in proportion to their bank take-home, stops funding goals from their own retirement year. Someone already retired keeps their share, because today’s left over already comes from their retirement income. A repayment that stops comes back in full while anyone still has an income. Dated-cost money after every payer’s working share stops becomes a cash capital requirement under retirement, funded before that boundary. A deficit is not reduced by retirement.
The opening central-policy reserve remains protected.
Goal-saving transfers are excluded from stated regular spending.
